boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Gannon study environments documented by university sources, from quiet library levels to campus lounges and reservable rooms.

cards.title: Nash Library Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring independent work and keep conversation to a minimum: Gannon identifies the third floor as the library’s silent floor.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent floor for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide identifies Nash Library’s third floor as a silent floor.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Nash Library; confirm current library building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Nash Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.notes: Set up here when a quieter library setting suits your work; Gannon classifies the second floor among its quieter areas.
cards.short_summary: A quieter library level for reading and concentrated coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide says the second and third floors of Nash Library are quieter areas.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Nash Library; confirm current library building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Nash Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.notes: Reserve a room when your project needs a defined workspace; Gannon reports rooms in multiple sizes for groups of two to 10.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms with configurations for small-group work.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s catalog states that Nash Library has 49 study rooms in configurations designed for two to 10 students.
cards.source_title: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.access_notes: Room availability and reservation procedures may apply; check with the Nash Library Service Desk.

cards.title: Nash Library First Floor
cards.subtitle: Nash Library and Student Learning Commons
cards.notes: Choose this level when you need access to the library’s more active environment, rather than the quieter upper floors.
cards.short_summary: An active-level library setting for coursework between tasks.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide describes Nash Library’s first floor and lower level as more active areas.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Nash Library; confirm current library building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Nash Library Courtyards
cards.subtitle: Outdoor seating at Nash Library
cards.notes: Use an outdoor table for reading or laptop work when weather permits; Gannon lists seating in the library’s courtyards.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor Nash seating for a change of setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide lists open seating in the courtyards at Nash Library.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: Outdoor setting; availability depends on weather and current campus access conditions.

cards.title: Waldron 219
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Waldron Campus Center
cards.notes: Check whether the room is unbooked before settling in; Gannon’s study guide lists Waldron 219 with 32 seats.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor Waldron room listed for study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide lists Waldron 219 as a 32-seat study space.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: This is an event-capable room; check for scheduled reservations before use.

cards.title: Hagerty Lounge
cards.subtitle: Outside Waldron 219, Waldron Campus Center
cards.notes: Use the lounge’s seating for a short work session, and keep an eye on event activity around nearby Waldron 219.
cards.short_summary: A Waldron lounge directly outside Room 219.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon identifies Hagerty Lounge as located directly outside Waldron 219 and lists it with 16 study seats.
cards.access_notes: Near an event space; seating may be affected by scheduled functions.

cards.title: Foreign Language Lounge
cards.subtitle: Room 2206, Palumbo Academic Center
cards.notes: Head to Palumbo Room 2206 for a smaller lounge setting; Gannon’s guide lists 12 seats in this named space.
cards.short_summary: A 12-seat named lounge in the Palumbo Academic Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon’s campus study-space guide lists the Foreign Language Lounge in Palumbo Room 2206 with 12 seats.
cards.source_title: A guide to study spaces on campus
cards.access_notes: Listed as open during class times in Gannon’s guide; verify current room availability before use.

cards.title: Commuter Corner
cards.subtitle: Palumbo Academic Center
cards.notes: Commuter students can use the two study rooms, tables, chairs and soft seating between classes; the space also has a kitchenette.
cards.short_summary: A commuter-focused Palumbo lounge with study rooms and seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon says the Commuter Corner has tables, chairs, soft seating, a kitchenette and two study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Designed for traditional commuter students; confirm eligibility and access with the Office of Commuter Life.

cards.title: Adult and Veteran Lounge
cards.subtitle: Room 3241, Palumbo Academic Center
cards.notes: Adult and military-affiliated students can use the comfortable seating and study areas for focused work or a reset between commitments.
cards.short_summary: A Palumbo lounge with study areas for adult and veteran students.
cards.evidence_claim: Gannon states that the Adult and Veteran Lounge in Palumbo Room 3241 includes comfortable seating and study areas and is open during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Gannon University Dedicates New Adult and Veteran Lounge with Blessing
cards.access_notes: Designed for adult learners and military-affiliated students; confirm eligibility and room access before visiting.
